llm_analysis.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
llm_analysis.takeaway: P$^{3}$-WAM targets egocentric dexterous manipulation by unifying three modes in one world action model: Perceive reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video, Predict generates visual futures under prescribed actions, and Plan jointly produces action trajectories with anticipated visual consequences from an image, language instruction, and optional visual goal. The method inserts a compact structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer via a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention, with randomized modality visibility. Reported evidence is that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation, and outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets. Inspect how the shared-weight mixture-of-transformers and modality visibility schedule affect cross-mode transfer.

llm_analysis.title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
llm_analysis.takeaway: FastVLA addresses inference efficiency in Vision-Language-Action models, where high-resolution multi-view images become hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency at each timestep. The training-free framework scores token importance through task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration, motivated by the observation that decision-critical tokens are task-determined and token budgets vary across steps. Evaluated on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot, it reports 35-59% LLM-backbone FLOPs reduction and 9-32% action latency reduction in simulation, and 20% end-to-end latency reduction on the real robot at comparable success. Inspect how the inverse-Simpson calibration behaves across task phases.

llm_analysis.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
llm_analysis.takeaway: DSP asks how robots can autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed for dexterous manipulation. A robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data for training a world model; at inference the same play policy guides model-predictive control by proposing candidate action sequences evaluated under that world model, and a closed-loop goal-conditioned policy is distilled through self-play within the world model to accelerate inference. Evaluated on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand in simulation and real world, it reports outperforming hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. Inspect the MPC candidate evaluation and self-play distillation loop.

paper.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
paper.summary: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

paper.title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
paper.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.

paper.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
paper.summary: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.
